module_title: Basics of Matter and the Three Classic States
introduction: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space (volume). Everything around us, from the air we breathe to the chair we sit on, is made of matter. Matter is made up of tiny, continuously moving particles called atoms and molecules.

core_concepts.title: Solid State
core_concepts.description:
Particles are tightly packed together with very strong intermolecular forces of attraction. 
Properties: They have a 'Fixed Shape' and 'Fixed Volume'. They are highly rigid and cannot be compressed easily. Example: Ice, Wood, Iron.

core_concepts.title: Liquid State
core_concepts.description:
Particles are loosely packed compared to solids. The forces of attraction are weaker, allowing particles to slide past one another. 
Properties: They have a 'Fixed Volume' but 'NO Fixed Shape' (they take the shape of the container). They can flow, so they are called fluids. Example: Water, Oil, Milk.

core_concepts.title: Gaseous State
core_concepts.description:
Particles are very far apart with negligible intermolecular forces. They move randomly at high speeds. 
Properties: They have 'NO Fixed Shape' and 'NO Fixed Volume'. They are highly compressible and expand to fill the entire space of any container. Example: Oxygen, Steam, Air.

core_concepts.title: Interconversion of States
core_concepts.description:
Matter can change from one physical state to another by altering temperature or pressure. 
1. Melting (Solid to Liquid). 
2. Boiling/Vaporization (Liquid to Gas). 
3. Condensation (Gas to Liquid). 
4. Freezing (Liquid to Solid).

important_entities.name: Compressibility of Gases
important_entities.significance: Because gases have large empty spaces between their particles, they can be highly compressed into small cylinders. This is the exact principle behind Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) used in our kitchens and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) in vehicles.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Are they exactly the same? No. A 'Gas' exists in the gaseous state at normal room temperature (like Oxygen or Nitrogen). A 'Vapour' is the gaseous form of a substance that is normally a liquid or solid at room temperature (like Water vapour or Camphor vapour).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Solid = Yes/Yes, Liquid = No/Yes, Gas = No/No
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Solids: Fixed Shape (Yes), Fixed Volume (Yes). Liquids: Shape (No), Volume (Yes). Gases: Shape (No), Volume (No).

exam_strategy_tips: A direct question in SSC exams: 'Which state of matter possesses the highest kinetic energy?' Answer: Gaseous state (because the particles are moving the fastest and most freely).
